blocking.section: Observability principles (O5) / Metrics catalog / Cardinality budget
blocking.issue: The document states a cardinality rule that one of its own families breaks. `ruralz_plugin_guest_events_total` takes `name` values that the guest chooses at runtime through `metric_add`. WASM plugin system admits the first 16 names a Plugin emits, so the values are user-supplied strings, unknown when the Revision compiles. They can also differ between Nodes if a Plugin derives names from traffic. That contradicts O5, the "never a label" rule and the claim that folding is identical on every Node. A contributor cannot tell which rule governs this family, and the cardinality table never counts it.
blocking.evidence: Line 40: "O5 | Bounded cardinality | Label values are Revision-bounded names or fixed enumerations, admitted at compile time"; line 123: "Never a label: ... or any user-supplied string"; line 548: "Every label value is known when a Revision compiles (O5) ... identically on every Node"; line 210: "accepts `ruralz_plugin_guest_events_total` (guest names are label values)". 05-wasm-plugin-system.md line 182: "`name` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, at most 16 per Plugin; a negative value or 17th name returns `ERR_LIMIT`."
blocking.fix: State the exception in O5 and in the Cardinality budget: guest event names are admitted at runtime, first come, at most 16 per Plugin Policy (so at most 16 × Plugin Policies series), may differ between Nodes, and are never folded into `_overflow` because the ABI already refuses a 17th name. Add the family to the cardinality table (for 50 Plugin Policies, 800 series (hypothesis)). Alternatively, add an Open question owned by wasm-plugin-system proposing that Plugins declare their event names, which would make them compile-time values.

blocking.issue: The memory and series budgets leave out the label sets that the document's own Hot Reload rule retains. Quotas apply per Revision (100,000 series). Dropped names stay exported until the snapshot that references them retires, and the CI test accepts up to three times the single-Revision worst case. Yet the Metrics memory budget holds only "at the series cap", and the Cluster bound of 10 million series uses the single-Revision figure. After a Revision that renames many Routes, a Node can legitimately hold about 3 × 100,000 series. By the document's own per-series assumptions that is roughly 55 to 60 MiB, over both the 24 MiB metrics budget and the 40 MiB total. An operator sizing a metrics store for a 100-Node Cluster would under-provision by up to three times during churn.
blocking.evidence: Line 548: "quotas (target) of 6,000 per counter or gauge family, 2,000 per histogram family and 100,000 series per Revision"; line 550: "a dropped name is exported until the last snapshot referencing it retires (active plus K = 2 retired ...) ... MUST stay within 3 times the single-Revision worst case (hypothesis)"; line 535: "24 MiB or less at the series cap (hypothesis)"; line 542: "40 MiB or less (hypothesis)"; line 562: "a 100-Node Cluster stays under 10 million series (hypothesis)".
blocking.fix: Choose one option and state it. (a) Make the cap per Node, covering live and retiring series together: "100,000 series per Node including retiring label sets (target); a new Revision's label sets beyond the remaining room fold until retired snapshots close". (b) Keep per-Revision quotas and restate the Metrics memory row and the total at three times the cap, with the Cluster series bound given for steady state and for churn. Either way, name `ruralz_telemetry_series{state="retiring"}` as the signal that shows the difference.
